findings.title: Substring check treats negated `!event.type:error` queries as error-focused
findings.body:
`_is_error_focused_query` lowercases the raw query string and checks whether it contains `"event.type:error"`. That substring also appears in the negation `!event.type:error`, in `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and in free text such as `message:"event.type:error"`.

For these discover-dataset queries in allowlisted projects, `count()` is rewritten to `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` even though the matched rows are not (or not only) errors. Transactions and other non-error rows have no meaningful `sample_weight`, so the chart silently shows wrong counts, typically 0 or undercounted.

The check should parse the query (e.g. with the event search parser) and require a positive `event.type:error` filter, not a substring match.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer `dataset` and `request.GET['query']` instead of the per-call dataset and query
findings.body:
`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check is called with the closed-over outer `dataset` and `request`. `_is_error_focused_query` then reads `request.GET['query']` rather than the query actually being executed.

In the dashboard split path, `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction")` and the ERROR_EVENTS split both run against discover. However, the decision is made against the outer metrics dataset, which always returns False, so error counts there are never upsampled.

Conversely, the upsampling verdict for any call reflects the user's original query string, not the modified split query. Results for the same widget can therefore differ depending on which code path served them.

Pass `scoped_dataset` and the effective `query` to the eligibility check.

findings.title: "Performance" cache adds a remote cache round-trip to every events-stats call, even for non-error datasets
findings.body:
`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` does `cache.get` (and `cache.set` on a miss) before checking the dataset. Every `_get_event_stats` call therefore hits the shared cache backend (memcached/redis), including spans, transactions, metrics, logs and RPC queries that can never be upsampled.

Dashboard split requests call `_get_event_stats` up to four times, so they pay several round-trips.

The value being cached is a single `options.get` lookup, which Sentry's options manager already serves from an in-process cache. The "optimization" replaces a local lookup with a network call and writes one cache key per distinct project-id combination.

Check `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` first and drop the extra cache layer, or at minimum short-circuit before touching the cache.

findings.title: Allowlist changes are served stale for 60s and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is unusable/never called
findings.body:
Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds per (org, project-set). The docstring says `invalidate_upsampling_cache` "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes", but nothing calls it.

It also cannot be called meaningfully. The allowlist is a single global option, and the cache is keyed on arbitrary combinations of project ids. An options change has no way to enumerate which keys to delete.

As a result, removing a project from the allowlist (e.g. because upsampled data is wrong) keeps producing upsampled counts for up to a minute across all workers. Adding one keeps returning raw counts for the same period. Mixed results within a dashboard are possible.

The key also embeds `hash(tuple(...))`, which can in principle collide between different project sets. Either remove the cache or key and invalidate it on the option value itself.

findings.title: `options.get(key, [])` passes `[]` as `silent`, not as a default; real option path is never tested
findings.body:
`OptionsManager.get(key, silent=False)` has no default-value parameter. The `[]` is interpreted as `silent=[]` and is not used as a fallback value.

If `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is not registered in this codebase, `options.get` raises `UnknownOption`. Because the helper is now called on every events-stats request, that would turn every request into a 500.

All new tests patch the whole `options` module, so the real lookup is never exercised. Drop the misleading second argument, ensure the option is registered, and add a test that does not mock `options`.

findings.title: Top-events ranking uses raw `count()` while the plotted series are upsampled
findings.body:
For top events, only `timeseries_columns` are transformed. `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)`, `orderby=self.get_orderby(...)` and `equations` still use plain `count()`.

The top-N groups are therefore chosen and ordered by raw (sampled) counts, while the plotted values are upsampled. Groups with different client sample rates can display in an order that contradicts their plotted values, and equations referencing `count()` mix raw and upsampled numbers.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` is exposed as a public function and changes the `count` result type to `number`
findings.body:
Unlike the neighbouring internal helpers, the new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is not marked `private=True`. Any user can call `upsampled_count()` directly in discover or errors queries, including against data where `sample_weight` is not populated. That makes an internal implementation detail part of the public query API.

It also declares `default_result_type="number"`, while `count()` is `integer`. The response meta for the `count` column now changes type for allowlisted projects, which affects frontend formatting and any API consumer relying on the type.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink/submodule `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: The PR adds `sentry-repo` as a subproject commit pointing at the base commit, with no `.gitmodules` entry. This is clearly an accidental artifact of a local checkout. It adds a broken submodule to the repository root, which can confuse clones, CI checkouts and tooling. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Docstrings/comments contradict actual caching behavior
findings.body:
The `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docstring says it "reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time… intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state". Its only caller caches the result for 60s, so this is false.

In the endpoint, "This cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution" and "late transformation ensures we use the most current schema assumptions" also describe nothing the code actually does. The decision is recomputed per `_get_event_stats` call, and `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` is a no-op alias.

The transform branches inside the `use_rpc` paths are dead code, because `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` always returns False for `spans_rpc`/`ourlogs`. These comments will mislead future maintainers.

findings.title: Main entry point and its caching are untested; key edge cases missing
